questions.question: You’re late for an important meeting and your colleague says, *'Oh no, I’m so sorry—my train was delayed again!'*. How would you respond if you wanted to express genuine sympathy and offer a practical suggestion?
options: Don’t worry about it; it happens all the time.
That’s really kind of you to say, but you should have left earlier.
I’m really sorry to hear that—you should take the next one and let me know when you arrive.
Well, at least you’re not the only one late today.
questions.answer: I’m really sorry to hear that—you should take the next one and let me know when you arrive.

questions.question: A friend asks, *'Would you like to go to that new café down the street for coffee? It’s supposed to be amazing!'*. How would you respond if you were unsure but wanted to show interest and ask for clarification?
options: Yes, that sounds perfect—I’ll meet you there at 3.
I don’t know about that café—I’ve never been there before.
I’d love to, but I’ve got plans at 3—maybe next week?
That sounds great, but I’ll pass—I’m too busy this week.
questions.answer: I don’t know about that café—I’ve never been there before.

questions.question: Your boss says, *'We need to discuss the project timeline before the deadline. Can you meet with me tomorrow at 10 a.m.?'*. How would you respond if you were unable to attend but wanted to offer an alternative time politely?
options: Yes, I’ll be there at 10 a.m. sharp—I’m ready to start.
I’m sorry, but I can’t make tomorrow—I’ll meet you at 2 p.m. instead.
That’s fine—I’ll just work on it at home and send it by email.
I don’t think that’s a good idea—I’ll handle it myself.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, but I can’t make tomorrow—I’ll meet you at 2 p.m. instead.

questions.question: At a formal dinner, your host says, *'Please, everyone, join me for a toast to our successful collaboration!'*. How would you respond if you wanted to express agreement and enthusiasm while maintaining a formal tone?
options: That’s a great idea—I’ll raise my glass!
I’m not sure about that—I prefer to keep things professional.
I don’t think toasting is appropriate here—let’s talk about the work instead.
I’ll pass—I’m not comfortable with that kind of thing.
questions.answer: That’s a great idea—I’ll raise my glass!

questions.question: A neighbour complains, *'I’ve been trying to get in touch with you about the noise from your party last night—it was really loud!'*. How would you respond if you wanted to apologise, explain, and take responsibility for the situation?
options: I’m sorry about that—I’ll make sure to be quieter next time.
That’s not true—I didn’t hear anything last night.
I didn’t mean to bother you—I’ll ask my friends to keep it down.
It wasn’t my fault—I was just having a good time.
questions.answer: I’m sorry about that—I’ll make sure to be quieter next time.
